In [[Four-dimensional space|four-dimensional]] [[euclidean geometry]], the '''tesseractic honeycomb''' is one of the three [[List of regular polytopes#Tessellations of Euclidean 4-space|regular]] space-filling [[tessellation]]s (or [[honeycomb (geometry)|honeycomb]]s), represented by [[Schläfli symbol]] {4,3,3,4}, and consisting of a packing of [[tesseract]]s (4-[[hypercube]]s). 

Its [[vertex figure]] is a [[16-cell]]. Two tesseracts meet at each cubic [[Cell (geometry)|cell]], four meet at each [[Square (geometry)|square]] [[Face (geometry)|face]], eight meet on each [[Edge (geometry)|edge]], and sixteen meet at each [[Vertex (geometry)|vertex]].

It is an analog of the [[square tiling]], {4,4}, of the plane and the [[cubic honeycomb]], {4,3,4}, of 3-space. These are all part of the [[hypercubic honeycomb]] family of tessellations of the form {4,3,...,3,4}. Tessellations in this family are [[Self-dual polytope|self-dual]].

==Coordinates ==
Vertices of this honeycomb can be positioned in 4-space in all integer coordinates (i,j,k,l).

== Sphere packing ==
Like all regular [[Hypercubic honeycomb|hypercubic honeycombs]], the tesseractic honeycomb corresponds to a [[sphere packing]] of edge-length-diameter spheres centered on each vertex, or (dually) inscribed in each cell instead. In the hypercubic honeycomb of 4 dimensions, vertex-centered 3-spheres and cell-inscribed 3-spheres will both fit at once, forming the unique regular [[Cubic crystal system|body-centered cubic]] lattice of equal-sized spheres (in any number of dimensions). Since the tesseract is [[Tesseract#Radial equilateral symmetry|radially equilateral]], there is exactly enough space in the hole between the 16 vertex-centered 3-spheres for another edge-length-diameter 3-sphere. (This [[16-cell honeycomb#D4_lattice|4-dimensional body centered cubic lattice]] is actually the union of two tesseractic honeycombs, in dual positions.)

This is the same densest known regular 3-sphere packing, with [[kissing number]] 24, that is also seen in the other two regular tessellations of 4-space, the [[16-cell honeycomb#D4 lattice|16-cell honeycomb]] and the [[24-cell honeycomb#Kissing number|24-cell-honeycomb]]. Each tesseract-inscribed 3-sphere kisses a surrounding shell of 24 3-spheres, 16 at the vertices of the tesseract and 8 inscribed in the adjacent tesseracts. These 24 kissing points are [[24-cell#Radially equilateral honeycomb|the vertices of a 24-cell]] of radius (and edge length) 1/2.

== Constructions ==
There are many different [[Wythoff construction]]s of this honeycomb. The most symmetric form is [[Regular polytope|regular]], with [[Schläfli symbol]] {4,3,3,4}. Another form has two alternating [[tesseract]] facets (like a checkerboard) with Schläfli symbol {4,3,3<sup>1,1</sup>}. The lowest symmetry Wythoff construction has 16 types of facets around each vertex and a prismatic product Schläfli symbol {&infin;}<sup>4</sup>. One can be made by [[sterication|stericating]] another.

== Related polytopes and tessellations ==
{{C4_honeycombs}}

{{B4 honeycombs}}

The [[24-cell honeycomb]] is similar, but in addition to the vertices at integers (i,j,k,l), it has vertices at half integers (i+1/2,j+1/2,k+1/2,l+1/2) of odd integers only. It is a half-filled [[body centered cubic]] (a checkerboard in which the red 4-cubes have a central vertex but the black 4-cubes do not).

The [[tesseract]] can make a regular tessellation of the [[N-sphere|4-sphere]], with three tesseracts per face, with Schläfli symbol {4,3,3,3}, called an ''order-3 tesseractic honeycomb''. It is topologically equivalent to the regular polytope [[penteract]] in 5-space.

The tesseract can make a regular tessellation of 4-dimensional [[hyperbolic space]], with 5 tesseracts around each face, with Schläfli symbol {4,3,3,5}, called an [[order-5 tesseractic honeycomb]].

The [[Ammann–Beenker tiling]] is an [[aperiodic tiling]] in 2 dimensions obtained by [[Aperiodic_tiling#Cut-and-project_method|cut-and-project]] on the tesseractic honeycomb along an eightfold rotational axis of symmetry.<ref>{{cite journal | author1=Baake, M. | author2=Joseph, D. | title = Ideal and Defective Vertex Configurations in the Planar Octagonal Quasilattice | journal = Physical Review B | year = 1990 | volume = 42 |issue=13 | pages = 8091–8102 | doi=10.1103/physrevb.42.8091 | pmid=9994979 | bibcode=1990PhRvB..42.8091B }}</ref><ref>Beenker, F.P.M. (1982). [https://research.tue.nl/en/publications/algebraic-theory-of-non-periodic-tilings-of-the-plane-by-two-simp/ "Algebraic theory of non-periodic tilings of the plane by two simple building blocks: a square and a rhombus"]. ''Eindhoven University of Technology''. EUT report. WSK, Dept. of Mathematics and Computing Science; Vol. 82-WSK-04.</ref>

=== Birectified tesseractic honeycomb ===
A [[birectified tesseractic honeycomb]], {{CDD|node_1|split1|nodes|4a4b|nodes}}, contains all rectified 16-cell ([[24-cell]]) facets and is the [[Voronoi tessellation]] of the [[16-cell honeycomb#D4 lattice|D<sub>4</sub><sup>*</sup> lattice]]. Facets can be identically colored from a doubled <math>{\tilde{C}}_4</math>×2, <nowiki>[[</nowiki>4,3,3,4]] symmetry, alternately colored from <math>{\tilde{C}}_4</math>, [4,3,3,4] symmetry, three colors from <math>{\tilde{B}}_4</math>, [4,3,3<sup>1,1</sup>] symmetry, and 4 colors from <math>{\tilde{D}}_4</math>, [3<sup>1,1,1,1</sup>] symmetry.
